detail.formulaSheet: The month sheet's Top Box cell: for each of the five questions, the share of its ratings that were 5, averaged over the five.
detail.formulaPooled: Every rating of 5 over every rating given, across the months and surveys in view. No sheet holds a figure this wide, and this is how the deck combines them — so each person counts once, whichever month they answered in.
detail.barsNote: Each bar above is that month sheet's own Top Box cell, shown as written.

detail.avgNoteOverall: Averaging the {months} monthly figures instead would give {value}, which lets a quiet month count as much as a busy one. The deck counts people, so this page does not.
detail.ratingsNote: Five questions per respondent, so one person leaves up to five ratings.

formulaText.firstTimeInstall: An installation scores 1 when no corrective-maintenance case names the same serial within {days} days after the installation's TimeLine end date; 0 when one does.
formulaText.firstTimeFix: A CM case scores 1 when no later CM names the same serial within {days} days of it being reported; 0 when one does.
formulaText.sla: The case was checked within the board's configured SLA days of being reported: RE Action date minus Open Date. Exactly the limit counts as within. No action date recorded means unknown, not a breach. Neither board has a close date, so this is time-to-first-action, not time-to-close.
formulaText.totalCmCases: Installations are counted in the month their TimeLine ends; CM cases in the month they were reported. Each board may name a category column (Job Type, Type of case) and the values that count as a KPI case; rows outside that list are synced and archived but not counted here.

apiNotes.bucketing: Installations are counted in the month their TimeLine ends; CM cases in the month they were reported.
apiNotes.matching: Both windows join on serial number alone, across boards. Tickets naming no serial cannot be matched and are counted as successes.
apiNotes.split: The installation board does not say which kind of robot a case concerns, so the serial is looked up among CM cases: the cleaning and delivery boards each handle one kind, so a serial seen on one of them identifies the robot. A case that still cannot be placed counts in the fleet total but in neither line.
apiNotes.category: Each board may name a category column and the values that count as a KPI case. Rows outside that list are synced and archived but not counted. A follow-up CM is still a follow-up whatever its category.
